# St. Thomas Energy Project Website

This website showcases the St. Thomas Energy Project, a 1.2MW solar installation with battery storage and grid integration capabilities.

## Project Overview

- **Location**: St. Thomas, [Region/Country]
- **Capacity**: 1.2MW solar + 2MWh battery storage
- **Annual Production**: 5,000 MWh
- **Homes Powered**: 50 average households
- **Grid Availability**: 98.5%

## Key Features

### Solar Power System
- 4,800 high-efficiency monocrystalline panels
- 8 acres of land coverage
- 20-year performance warranty
- Annual CO2 reduction: [X] tons

### Battery Storage
- 2MWh lithium-ion battery system
- 500kW peak discharge capability
- 4-hour backup duration
- Grid stabilization and peak shaving

### Grid Integration
- Seamless bidirectional power flow
- Demand response program participation
- Peak demand reduction: 15%
- Critical infrastructure backup

## Technical Specifications

### Solar Array
- Panel Type: Monocrystalline
- Efficiency: 20.5%
- Tilt Angle: 25 degrees
- Azimuth: 180 degrees (South-facing)
- Inverter Type: String inverters with MPPT

### Battery System
- Chemistry: Lithium Iron Phosphate (LiFePO4)
- Round-trip Efficiency: 95%
- Cycle Life: 6,000 cycles @ 80% DoD
- Warranty: 10 years

### Grid Connection
- Connection Voltage: 480V three-phase
- Protection: Islanding detection, overcurrent protection
- Monitoring: Real-time SCADA system
- Communication: Modbus TCP/IP
